messages:
maria: noticed a spike in KV cache evictions right after last deploy, p99 token latency up ~30% for affected endpoints. can we stand up a quick war-room? i can be there in 10.
deploy-bot: deploy v3.14.2 to service/kv-cache finished at 1769990160 by james — diff: https://git.redwood/changes/kv-cache-3.14.2 :hammer_and_wrench:
james: i'm free, i pushed the change that adjusted the eviction heuristic. suspect we under-estimated memory footprint for long prompt workloads.
arjun: i'll join the call. can someone drop a bridge? also posting quick query to get affected node ids: `SELECT node_id, evictions, last_gc FROM kv_metrics WHERE evictions > 100 ORDER BY evictions DESC LIMIT 20;`
emily: joining. grabbing logs now — running `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=kv-cache --tail=200` to look for OOM/gc messages.
maria: agenda on the fly: 1) confirm rollback vs config tweak, 2) pin down the offending workload, 3) apply hotfix (fallback policy) or rollback, 4) postmortem owners.
rachel-oncall: bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridge/zk-evict-176999 — in 5. put any quick troubleshooting steps here so folks can run while others join.
mike: quick hint — if it's a long-prompt tail call pattern, prefix cache isn't helping. check `cache_prefix_miss_rate` metric and `kv_cache.size_bytes` per node.
arjun: see spike on node i-0a3b: evictions 1.2k, last_gc=1769989800. config shows `max_entries=50k` but avg entry size jumped. suspect serialization change in the model client.
ames: (typo) james: ^ i meant to say also check serializer version in the client release that was deployed. i bumped proto v2 which changes layout.
emily: here's filtered log snippet showing repeated `serialize: large object > 1.2MB` errors:
```
2026-03-16T21:22:10Z kv-cache[pid=233] WARN serialize: truncated payload, len=1285480
2026-03-16T21:22:10Z kv-cache[pid=233] INFO eviction triggered, evicted=27, reason=mem_pressure
```
maria: decision? options: rollback deploy v3.14.2 now (fast) OR apply hotfix to cap serialized size and drop huge keys (safer immediate). thoughts?
james: i'd vote rollback to buy time and then ship a serializer fix + integration test. i can trigger rollback if we agree.
arjun: rollback + postmortem + tests. i'll draft the repro.
emily: rolling back sounds good. i'll prepare a canary check script to validate no more evictions after rollback.
rachel-oncall: james, please run rollback and post the rollback commit/ID here. after rollback we'll watch metrics for 10m then decide next steps. i'm taking incident lead.
james: rolling back now — `deployctl rollback service/kv-cache --to=3.14.1 --reason="eviction-regression"` (started).
deploy-bot: rollback started for service/kv-cache to 3.14.1 by james at 1769991562 — status: in_progress.
emily: canary script (run locally): `for n in {1..50}; do curl -sS https://kv.internal/health || echo fail; sleep 2; done` — will post results.
maria: thanks everyone — we'll capture notes in the ticket (#INC-3421) and schedule a short RFC review for the serializer change tomorrow. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully at 1769991780 — service/kv-cache now at 3.14.1.
rachel-oncall: watching metrics — evictions down 92% in first 4m. leaving the bridge open for 15 more minutes for any follow-ups.
james: posting rollback commit id: abc1234. follow-up PR to add size cap to serializer is in draft (WIP).
arjun: i'll own the postmortem section on root cause and tests. assigning to myself and james.
maria: closing war-room in 10 unless anyone else needs more time. great work moving fast. :raised_hands:
